title: Cohorted shadow replay with heuristic safety latches and deterministic rollback
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: We need a lightweight, deterministic way to validate candidate model variants against production traffic without committing user-visible traffic immediately. Existing shadowing proved noisy for cohorted traffic and lacked a compact mechanism for deterministic rollback when regressions were detected. This PR introduces a Cohorted Shadow Replay controller: it samples production cohorts, replays them to candidate variants under configurable fidelity, and attaches heuristic safety latches (latency/cost/error gates + time-windowed anomaly detectors) that can trigger an automated deterministic rollback AND create a snapshot for forensic replay.

What this PR does (summary): adds a new rollout controller (cohorted-shadow-replay-controller) that: 1) defines cohort selectors and sampling profiles; 2) streams sampled requests (optionally anonymized) to shadow targets with consistent session-affinity; 3) performs batched deterministic replays to avoid interference with live throughput; 4) evaluates compare metrics (latency P95, token-level divergence score, error-rate, cost-per-token) over sliding windows; 5) exposes policy hooks for automatic rollback, pause, or escalate to on-call; 6) writes compact snapshots for failed cohorts to S3-compatible storage for offline bisect and replay.

Key design notes: - Cohort selectors accept boolean predicates based on route, header flags, user segments, or synthetic tags. - Replay fidelity modes: dry-run (no response compare), sample-compare (compare summaries), and full-compare (token-level alignment). - Safety latches combine threshold gates with short-term anomaly detectors (EWMA + robust outlier trimming) and require quorum across multiple metrics before auto-rollback. - Rollback is implemented as a transactional operation: controller writes a rollback marker and issues an atomic traffic swap via existing promote/swap API; if swap fails, controller falls back to a soft-quarantine (shadow-only) and alerts. - Snapshots are compact (request metadata + hash + minimal context) and encrypted with KMS keys when Private deployment is enabled.

Files changed (high level): added controller implementation in rollout/controller/cohorted_shadow_replay.go, new protobuf messages in proto/rollout/v1/replay.proto, CRD/schema updates in deploy/k8s/rollout-crd.yaml, a new e2e test harness under test/rollout/cohort_replay_test.go, migration docs in docs/rollouts/cohorted_replay.md, and console wiring for a Replays tab in console/src/components/Rollouts/ReplayPanel.tsx. Small changes to the promote API to accept a signature token for transactional rollback.

Test plan: unit tests for core controller logic and gate evaluation (added ~40 unit tests), integration tests that run a synthetic cohort against a canary candidate in CI harness (simulated traffic, deterministic assertions on metrics), e2e in the benchmark-lab to validate mutexing with hot paths. Local smoke steps included in docs; CI added two new checks: rollout-unit and rollout-integration.

Backward compatibility & migration: existing rollout CRs are unchanged unless they opt into the new Replay profile. The new CRD field 'replayPolicy' is optional with sane defaults (sampling: 1%, fidelity: sample-compare, autoRollback: false). For Dedicated/Private customers with stricter privacy requirements, snapshot encryption and in-cluster-only replay are available via flags in the CR.

Operational notes & rollout plan: feature gated behind rollout.experimental=true. We'll enable gradually: (1) internal canaries for platform teams, (2) small external beta with two customers (opt-in), (3) wider availability after 3 weeks of telemetry. Metrics surfaced: replay_request_count, replay_error_count, replay_token_divergence, replay_auto_rollback_count.

Why this is different: unlike prior shadowing approaches which mirrored 100% of traffic and relied on ad-hoc analysis, this controller focuses on reproducible, cohort-localized replays with deterministic rollback and compact forensic artifacts, improving both operator confidence and cost efficiency.

Related: ENG-3421 (cohort sampling service), ENG-3987 (rollback transaction semantics), SUP-2123 (customer incident that motivated deterministic snapshots).

review_conversation: Connor Blake: This looks promising. Two questions: how do we guarantee session affinity across replay vs live for stateful models?
Maya Chen: We attach a deterministic session-hash to the replay stream and pin it to the same model shard key used in production routing. Added details in cohorted_shadow_replay.go comments.
Anika Shah: Need clear SLO impacts and backpressure behavior if replay queue grows. Add quotas and backpressure hooks.
Maya Chen: Implemented queue-size soft-limit and backpressure signal to throttle sampling rate; documented in docs/rollouts/cohorted_replay.md. CI integration tests simulate queue pressure.
Luis Ortega: Gate evaluation looks susceptible to false positives on transient cloud noise; consider requiring a 2-period confirmation.
Maya Chen: Safety latches now require metric quorum plus a stable-window confirmation (configurable, default 2 windows).
Connor Blake: Approving pending one small nit on proto naming (ReplaySnapshot -> SnapshotRecord).
Maya Chen: Renamed ReplaySnapshot to SnapshotRecord and updated consumers.
release_notes: Adds a cohorted shadow replay controller for deterministic sampled replays, automatic rollback hooks with heuristic safety latches, compact encrypted snapshots for forensic replay, and console UI for replay monitoring. Feature is behind experimental gate and opt-in via new CRD fields.
changelog_entry: Feature: cohorted shadow replay controller (experimental) — controlled sampling, deterministic replays, auto-rollback with snapshotting; see docs/rollouts/cohorted_replay.md for usage and migration.
notes_for_ops: Enable rollout.experimental=true to try. Watch replay_auto_rollback_count and replay_token_divergence. For Private installs, ensure KMS is configured for snapshots or set in-cluster-only=true to avoid external storage.
